newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share punters focus on Thailand, OTCs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share punters focus on Thailand, OTCs.

text.p: Singapore stock market punters switched to Malaysian over-the-counter issues on hopes a rise in nearby Thai stocks would trigger spillover demand.
"Malaysia was seen as the natural market to gain from the jump in Thai stocks," a foreign brokerage dealer said.
Thai stocks reacted negatively at first to news the baht would be subject to a "managed float" immediately.
But it bounced sharply later as investors felt the flotation might be the last of many bearish factors.
At the lunch break, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 2.17 points at 1,979.11.
But the UOB OTC index tracking Malaysian stocks traded over-the-counter rose 8.24 points to 1,142.88.
Institutions remained mostly cautious but were selectively nibbling on blue chips and small capitalisation issues.
Dealers said they were more wary of baht volatility and any change to U.S. interest rates, although this was not expected from the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Wednesday.
Actives included new stocks China-linked Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical TIAN.SI, up three cents to US$1.13 and Raffles Medical Group, up six cents to Singapore $0.98.
SIA nudged slightly higher to S$7.30, up five cents, encouraged by its joint venture with aircraft-engine maker of the U.S., Pratt & Whitney.
